suggested_query: U.S. Southern Command counter-narcotics lethal force rules of engagement and legal framework—when can forces kill without judicial process in international waters
reason: The Caribbean vessel strike killing four people was reported as routine enforcement, suggesting an operational framework that authorizes lethal force without the due process required domestically. Understanding the legal architecture that permits extrajudicial killing as counter-narcotics policy reveals how accountability thresholds vary based on operational classification rather than the severity of state action.
